clauses.current_legal_basis: The ordering lead of EO 12014 continues because the order states no end and no instrument revoking it was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The ordering lead recites the President's authority under the Constitution and statutes and introduces the abolition and amendment that follow. It states no end and no held instrument revokes the order, so it remains in force on 2026-10-14 together with the amendment it introduces.

clauses.mechanism: performed on issuance (own terms: the Board is hereby abolished)
clauses.reason: The order provides that the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board is hereby abolished. That command was performed on issuance, October 19, 1977 (the signing date printed under the order and the Federal Register filing date, 42 FR 56105), so the clause is spent from that date; the Board has no continuing existence to which the clause could apply. This is performance by the order's own terms, not an end imposed by a later instrument.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The new Sections 3 and 4 of Executive Order 10717 inserted by this order continue, as amended by Executive Order 12107 to name the Office of Personnel Management, because no instrument ending Executive Order 10717 or the insertion was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14.

later_events.mechanism: amendment (section 2-101 substitutes Office of Personnel Management and its Director for Civil Service Commission and its Chairman in Executive Orders 10717 and 12014; effective January 1, 1979 under section 2-404)

clauses.reason: The clause amends Executive Order No. 10717, as amended, by deleting Sections 3 to 9 and adding new Sections 3 and 4, under which the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission advises and assists the President in selecting recipients of the President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service, nominations are made on the principles in Section 4(a) to (c), and persons appointed by the President are not eligible unless in the opinion of the Commission they are currently serving in a career position. The amendment was performed on issuance and its text continues as part of Executive Order 10717 as amended. Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, January 3, 1979; signed December 28, 1978) section 2-101 lists Executive Orders 10717 and 12014 and amends each by substituting Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission and Director of the Office of Personnel Management for Chairman, effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends; no held instrument revokes Executive Order 10717 or the amendment, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14 with the Office of Personnel Management and its Director in place of the Commission and its Chairman.

research_rationale:
Read the held Federal Register text of EO 12014 (42 FR 56105, October 21, 1977; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12014.txt) in full. In one sentence it abolishes the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board and amends Executive Order 10717 (the President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service) by deleting Sections 3 to 9 and adding new Sections 3 and 4. The prepared inventory is one clause for the whole body; it is corrected to three clauses by characters (ordering lead, abolition, amendment) because the abolition is a one-time act. The held Federal Register text of Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055) lists Executive Orders 10717 and 12014 in its section 2-101 and substitutes the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission in each, effective January 1, 1979; it is a later amendment, not an end, and the dossier flagged it as an unlocated target provision because the list falls on a later page than the section heading. The held corpus search for Executive Order 10717 finds the 1989 codification, Executive Orders 10979 and 11085 (earlier amendments of 10717 that predate this order's rewrite of its Sections 3 to 9), a current 5 CFR 451.203 sentence that the Office of Personnel Management reviews recommendations 'in accordance with Executive Order 10717, as amended', and no revocation. The three bounded machine searches were read (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) and show no instrument ending the order. The abolition is spent by performance on issuance, and the amendment is operative on 2026-10-14. Limits: the U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14; the 5 CFR sentence is a lead and is not relied on as a legal basis.

savings.reason: EO 12014 has no savings or transitional provision. The effect of the abolition (the Board no longer exists) is a completed consequence, and the functions it exercised were reassigned by the new Section 3 as amended by Executive Order 12107.
